claims: The patient is currently on an antiretroviral regimen including lamivudine / zidovudine, efavirenz, and rifampicin isoniazid pyrazinamide and ethambutol [4][5], which aligns with standard HIV treatment protocols.

Rifampicin-based regimens are often used for co-infection management or specific drug interactions; however, the patient's recent hemoglobin of 3.9 g/dL on 2025-12-14 [104] is critically low and requires urgent clinical attention to rule out severe anemia.

The repeated orders for chest X-rays (2025-10-23, 2025-12-14) and the patient's active tuberculosis treatment program status [1] suggest ongoing monitoring of pulmonary involvement or progression of TB disease.
Monitoring of renal function via serum creatinine [308] is standard practice when patients are on multi-drug regimens to ensure there is no drug-induced nephrotoxicity.

claims: The patient is currently on an antiretroviral regimen including lamivudine / zidovudine, efavirenz, and rifampicin isoniazid pyrazinamide and ethambutol [4][5], which aligns with standard HIV treatment protocols.

Rifampicin-based regimens are often used for co-infection management or specific drug interactions; however, the patient's recent hemoglobin of 3.9 g/dL on 2025-12-14 [104] is critically low and requires urgent clinical attention to rule out severe anemia.

The repeated orders for chest X-rays (2025-10-23, 2025-12-14) and the patient's active tuberculosis treatment program status [1] suggest ongoing monitoring of pulmonary involvement or progression of TB disease.
Monitoring of renal function via serum creatinine [308] is standard practice when patients are on multi-drug regimens to ensure there is no drug-induced nephrotoxicity.
